title: Rethinking Metrics for Lexical Semantic Change Detection

selection.evidence: Found 2026-11-24 in a literature scan for arena-lsc (LChange'26 proceedings); flagged in the stewardship log 11-24 and 11-25 as 'not in the KB; graded change, not the arena's 1b'. Opened 2026-11-26 for the arena paper's related work, before any suspicion about its results.

cost.compute_notes: PDF (12 pp incl. appendix A) read in full from page images; appendices B-D not read. Reanalysis on CPU with XL-LEXEME embeddings already on disk for arena-lsc (DWUG EN/DE/SV in the SemEval-2027 Task 3 format): amd_check.py ~15 min, period_blind.py ~2 min. Authors' code (github.com/roksanagow/Rethinking_LSCD_Metrics) not cloned.

triggers: AMD SAMD average minimum distance semantic change metric
APD vs PRT which graded change metric
does APD measure polysemy rather than change
semantic change metric under PCA dimensionality reduction

claims.statement: Averaged over eight LSCD datasets (SemEval-2020 EN/DE/SV/LA, LSCDiscovery ES, NorDiaChange x2, Chinese) and all encoders, Spearman with graded change on FULL embeddings: APD .405, PRT .395, AMD .442, SAMD .444; AMD in the definition space .519; under per-word PCA AMD .542, SAMD .550 (APD .190, PRT .093). Correspondence metrics are 'the best performance and the most stable'.
claims.scope: Figure 2; std in brackets is across languages x encoders (.12-.27). No significance test or per-dataset uncertainty is reported; datasets have 31-100 words, where one Spearman has a standard error near 0.15.

our_assessment.why: With XL-LEXEME on DWUG EN/DE/SV (46/50/44 words, cluster-JSD gold) the FULL-space differences vs APD are AMD -0.05/+0.02/-0.00 and SAMD -0.02/+0.02/-0.01, every 95% bootstrap CI spans 0 (reanalysis/amd_check.json). The averaged advantage is driven by weak non-specialised encoders, where all metrics are low; it is not shown with uncertainty.

claims.statement: With XL-LEXEME, SAMD on per-word PCA reaches .694 averaged over languages, above APD (.635) and PRT (.643) on full embeddings; AMD and SAMD stay robust under PCA and random dimension selection while APD and PRT degrade.
claims.scope: Section 4 'Specialised encoder' and Figure 3; K (PCA components) = the number of LLM-generated definitions for that word (EN 11, DE 3.75, SV 4.26 on average, Table 1).

our_assessment.why: Not reproduced at K = 4 on DWUG EN/DE/SV with XL-LEXEME: SAMD_PCA4 .44/.63/.32 vs APD_FULL .79/.83/.87, and AMD collapses under PCA (.16/.33/.11) rather than staying robust. Scope differs (fixed K = 4 vs the paper's per-word K; DWUG conversions with cluster-JSD gold vs the official SemEval graded scores), so 'disputed', not 'refuted'.

claims.statement: On DWUG EN/DE/SV with XL-LEXEME, most of APD's graded-change correlation is period-blind: the word's mean pairwise usage distance with periods ignored (dispersion) gives Spearman .74/.80/.87 against APD's .79/.83/.87; APD with period labels permuted within word gives .74/.80/.87; the gold number of senses alone gives .77/.42/.91. APD beats dispersion only on EN, +0.05 [+0.001, +0.137]. Gold-only: Spearman(gold JSD, entropy of the pooled sense distribution, periods ignored) .88/.85/.97.
claims.scope: Two-period sets, cluster-JSD gold computed from the DWUG clusterings (gold JSD itself grows with the number of senses), one encoder. The period-specific part (APD minus dispersion) still correlates .59/.75/.57, so APD does carry change signal; the headline number does not isolate it.

our_assessment.why: Own measurement with a known-answer control (within-word period shuffle) and a gold-only check: the gold change score is nearly a function of pooled sense entropy, which polysemy and change raise alike, so two-period sets of this kind cannot separate them; a high APD correlation is not evidence of change modelling. Corrected 2026-11-26 (same day) from 'rewards polysemy/dispersion', which overclaimed the causal direction. Any graded-change metric comparison (this paper's included) should report the period-shuffled score beside the real one.
